checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any readmissions, with reasons and discharge summaries.
Falls and near-falls: count and document any falls, injuries, or syncope in the window; note orthostatic symptoms given recent antihypertensive changes and the patient's age of 86.

Blood pressure trend since the last review: review all readings, including orthostatic readings if taken, against the regimen changes started 2026-07-19 (amlodipine 2.5 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg added together on that date, alongside existing metoprolol succinate 100 mg). Flag hypotension, dizziness, or readings outside the team's target range for prescriber review.

Medication reconciliation: confirm all seven active medications and their adherence; identify any starts, stops, or dose changes in the window beyond the 2026-07-19 antihypertensive additions; check whether the three new agents were titrated or stopped and whether any were discontinued early.

Renal and electrolyte monitoring: because lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide were started together in July 2026 and the patient has diabetes, check for any post-start creatinine, potassium, and sodium labs in the window and whether they were ordered and resulted; flag any overdue monitoring.

Glycemic status and diabetes care: review glucose readings, HbA1c timing, and whether any diabetes medications were started or stopped; the active list shows no glucose-lowering agent, so confirm whether this is intentional and documented, and check for hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia events.
Neuropathy and foot care: document any foot ulcers, infections, new numbness, or pain; check whether podiatry or foot exam is due.
Recurrent UTI: count UTI diagnoses, antibiotic courses, and urinalysis or culture results in the window; note any new urinary symptoms, incontinence, or confusion that could signal infection.

Cardiac and antiplatelet review: confirm ischemic heart disease follow-up, any chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin spray use, and bleeding or bruising while on clopidogrel plus the other agents; confirm lipid and statin status given simvastatin 20 mg since 2008 and hypertriglyceridemia history.

Anemia and weight: review hemoglobin trend and any iron or bleeding workup; review weight trend and BMI given obesity history and metabolic syndrome; check function and ADL/IADL changes, cognition screen, mood and social engagement, attendance at any programs, and caregiver status; list any care-plan items due in the window (assessments, consent or advance-directive review, caregiver check-in).
